mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for two consecutive weeks after bottoming at t-1w (-23.0 to -20.1), indicating the trough of the Omicron-driven mobility contraction has passed. This own-series momentum should continue, driving the 4-week mean higher than the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -23.0 at t-1w to -20.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat/negative for the next two weekly readings despite the t-1w to t-0w uptick, i.e. next-4-week mean is not greater than last-4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rebound in WORKPLACES (from -47.6 at t-2w to -20.9 at t-0w, a 26.7 point recovery) signals restored commuting activity. Once the two-week change in WORKPLACES exceeds +15 points, commute-adjacent retail footfall rises within two weeks, lifting RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 15 points over two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise (or falls) in the two weeks following a WORKPLACES increase exceeding 15 points, breaking the commute-driven linkage.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both recovering simultaneously from their t-2w troughs; their joint recovery amplifies RETAIL_REC growth beyond what either series alone would predict, because combined commuting and transit use restores foot traffic near retail corridors.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -36.7 (t-2w) to -29.0 (t-0w) while WORKPLACES rose from -47.6 to -20.9
regime_hint: joint reopening of commuting and transit systems
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean does not exceed its last-4-week mean even though both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rose together, indicating no amplification effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL remains elevated (11.1 to 14.9 range, well above pre-period baseline) indicating sustained precautionary time-at-home behavior during the Omicron wave. This behavioral caution suppresses discretionary retail visits even as other categories partially recover, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above +11 for the last two weeks despite RETAIL_REC partial recovery
regime_hint: pandemic wave peak with persistent caution
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean rises above its last-4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above 11 points, falsifying the caution-suppression link.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous bottoming-out and recovery across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS between t-2w and t-0w suggests a coordinated loosening of pandemic restrictions (e.g., reduced capacity limits, lifted work-from-home mandates). This policy relaxation mechanically permits greater retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: at least three of WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, PARKS simultaneously improve for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:all three categories troughed at t-2w and rose through t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean remains lower than its last-4-week mean despite the broad-based recovery across WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS, indicating no policy-driven retail effect.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-January reflects the tail end of post-holiday normalization, when retail mobility typically continues a short-term seasonal decline for one more week before stabilizing, independent of pandemic dynamics, due to depleted post-holiday shopping demand.
candidate_trigger: decision date falls within the first three weeks of January
evidence_refs: fact:decision time point is 2022-01-15, within the post-holiday seasonal window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following the decision point rather than declining, contradicting the expected seasonal lull.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 points (a meaningful retreat from its t-2w peak of 14.9), it signals reduced precautionary home-bound behavior, which would permit RETAIL_REC to rise over the subsequent two weeks as households resume discretionary outings.
regime_hint: transition out of acute wave caution
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 points but RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean does not exceed its last-4-week mean, rejecting the threshold linkage.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM, an essential-activity proxy, has begun recovering faster than RETAIL_REC (from -8.4 at t-1w to -1.1 at t-0w, nearly back to baseline) while RETAIL_REC lags. This lead-lag relationship implies essential shopping normalization precedes and predicts a subsequent uptick in discretionary retail activity within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by more than 5 points week-on-week while RETAIL_REC lags behind
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -8.4 to -1.1 while RETAIL_REC rose only from -23.0 to -20.1 over the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM improvement exceeding 5 points, indicating no lead-lag relationship between essential and discretionary mobility.
